module_title: Reform Movements - Reformist vs. Revivalist, and South Indian Movements
introduction: This advanced level provides an analytical study of the ideological differences between movements (Reformist vs. Revivalist), the strong anti-Brahmin/anti-caste movements of South India (SNDP, Self-Respect Movement), and reforms within the Sikh and Parsi communities.

core_concepts.title: Reformist vs. Revivalist Ideologies
core_concepts.description: Reformists (e.g., Brahmo Samaj, Aligarh Movement) wanted to harmonize religion with modern science and Western ideas. Revivalists (e.g., Arya Samaj, Deoband) believed that the decline in religion was due to Western influence, aiming to return to the 'pure' ancient roots (Vedas/Quran).

core_concepts.title: SNDP Yogam (Kerala)
core_concepts.description: Started by Sri Narayana Guru for the upliftment of the Ezhava community (considered untouchables). His famous slogan was: 'One Religion, One Caste, One God for mankind'.

core_concepts.title: Self-Respect Movement (1925)
core_concepts.description: Started by E.V. Ramaswamy Naicker (Periyar) in Tamil Nadu. It was a fierce anti-Brahmin movement that strongly criticized Hindu scriptures (like Manusmriti) and promoted weddings without Brahmin priests.

core_concepts.title: Sikh Reforms: Akali Movement (1920s)
core_concepts.description: Also known as the 'Gurdwara Reform Movement'. Its objective was to free Sikh Gurdwaras from the control of corrupt and pro-British 'Mahants'. This eventually led to the formation of the SGPC (Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee) in 1925.

core_concepts.title: Rahnumai Mazdayasan Sabha (Parsi Reform)
core_concepts.description: Founded in 1851 by Dadabhai Naoroji, Naoroji Furdonji, and others. Its goal was to restore the Zoroastrian religion to its pristine purity and improve the social status of Parsi women.

important_entities.name: E.V. Ramaswamy Naicker (Periyar)
important_entities.significance: He published a journal named 'Kudi Arasu' and ran aggressive campaigns for social equality.

important_entities.name: D.K. Karve
important_entities.significance: Worked for the upliftment of widows in Maharashtra and established India's first women's university (SNDT Women's University) in Bombay in 1916.

important_entities.name: Sahodaran Ayyappan
important_entities.significance: He radically altered Narayana Guru's slogan to state: 'No Religion, No Caste, No God for mankind'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: The Dual Character of Arya Samaj
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Arya Samaj was ideologically 'Revivalist' (Go back to the Vedas), but socially it was entirely 'Reformist' because it supported women's education and strongly opposed child marriage.
The SNDP movement was not pan-Indian; it was fundamentally restricted to the Ezhava community of 'Kerala', though its ideological impact resonated widely.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The Gujarati journal 'Rast Goftar' (Truth Teller), started by Dadabhai Naoroji, was the main mouthpiece of the Parsi reform movement.

exam_strategy_tips: In Assertion-Reasoning type questions, thoroughly understand the fundamental ideological differences between 'Reformist' and 'Revivalist' movements.
Slogans (Quotes) from South Indian movement leaders (like Periyar and Sri Narayana Guru) are directly asked in UPSC and State PCS examinations.
